payload.question: What sustains an institutions existence over time in this ontology?
payload.answer: According to this ontology, an institution's existence over time is sustained by several interrelated factors grounded in recognition. Key sustaining mechanisms include: (1) InstitutionalSustainment (BFO_0000016/BFO_0000015) — a disposition and process that maintains the institution; (2) RecognitionDependence (BFO_0000016/BFO_0000019) — institutions depend ontologically on ongoing recognition; (3) CollectiveMaintenance (BFO_0000015) — collective acts by agents upholding the institution; (4) ParticipantIndependentPersistence (BFO_0000019) — the institution persists independently of particular individual participants changing (MembershipTurnoverInvariance); (5) InstitutionalPersistence (BFO_0000019) — a quality of enduring over time; (6) SustainingInstitutionalRelation (BFO_0000016) — relational dependencies that hold the institution together; (7) RecognitionStabilization (BFO_0000016/BFO_0000019) — stabilization of recognition patterns; (8) IntersubjectiveSustainmentProcess (BFO_0000015) — intersubjective processes continuously sustaining the institution; and (9) OngoingRecognitionProcess (BFO_0000015) — continuous recognition acts. The overarching thesis (CollectiveMaintenanceExistenceThesis) holds that collective maintenance by agents is what keeps institutions in existence, and InstitutionalDurability emerges from this sustained recognition network.
